For those of you just tuning in, welcome to Prompt of the Day. POTD is a subverse that tries to inspire creative writing through picture prompts. Once a week, we have a special user requested "Challenge Prompt." Challenge Prompts follow a certain set of guidelines and attempt to focus in on areas that the users need help on.

Here are the previous two challenges:

ChaP1 Create a Fantasy World

ChaP2 physical effects of emotions

This week's challenge genre was requested by /u/oaken. We were discussing a rather sharp decline in scary story quality. Oaken then asked if I could make a horror/spooky/creepy prompt.

THE CHALLENGE GUIDELINES

I thought long about how to set this one up. I could have said "you are alone at night... you hear a thud." -- something to that effect. The more I changed it, the more bored I got, so your prompt is "Make us afraid to go to bed at night." To help you do this I just have a few criteria:

  1. Make use of the senses. Really put your reader in the moment there. Is the fire crackling? What about the sweet aroma of lightly burnt wood and the sharp scent of pines? Sensory detail is important in this one. Or...lack of sensory detail.

  2. if you wish to make a longer post and story set up the lore around it. Doesn't have to be 20 pages long, but give just enough details to let your reader know what's going on.

  3. I want to believe. Have fun with it, and expect a good plethora of comments coming from our nearly 60 new members!

Happy Hauntings,

I'm wrote a poem! I'm still new to writing subs though, so this is one of my first attempts. Any feedback would be appreciated. :)

--

Under trees of shadow – crimson fire

Around – three women with faces like geese

And then they see the travelling squire

-

Knowing not his situation dire

He studies them – eyeing their tattered fleece

Then joins them around their crimson fire

-

A glance at roasting meat – drools desire

Dripping down is a waterfall of grease

What’s the meat – enquires famished squire

-

No great matter – have some of it sire

At one go – he snatches many a piece

Then puts a chunk over crimson fire

-

Belly full – he’s going to retire

He drifts off to sleep – utterly at peace

And then snores start coming from the squire

-

One of them nods at the blazing pyre

They hoist him up – but he is still at ease

They cackle, more meat for crimson fire

And then start cooking the sleeping squire

--

Edits: Formatting :/

Wow, I really enjoyed this piece. The ABA rhyme scheme really adds a sense of disquiet (something odd about that arrhythmic alternation) without sacrificing lyricism. Perhaps the pentameter had something to do with that?

The poem also provides an excellent level of detail. Enough clues for me to fill in all the peripheral information, immaculate imagery, and to top it all off, you have a fitting conclusion.

A masterful work. Not much criticism I can offer with my limited poetic experience, but my layman's ear gives hearty praises.
Awesome! It's great to see more poetry around this sub!

Shadow in the Night: Part 1

I’d love to tell you that everything worked out fine.

I’d love to tell you that I am completely sane.

I’d love to tell you that we are all safe.

But the truth is... I don’t know. Huddled in my apartment, I search the web for answers. My doors are locked - not that the locks help, but it gives me some peace of mind. I need peace of mind. I feel like I’m losing myself. I feel cold. I can remember when it began... I wish I had paid attention. I wish - no, no, it’s too late for wishing now. I can feel my hands trembling, the air in the apartment getting colder. I can feel the pricks of goosebumps on my arm, the fine hairs standing on end.

I was never one for religion, but the tapping and scratching on my window, three stories high, causes me to break down and pray.

It started about a month ago, just shy of the 30 day mark. I was suffering from terrible nightmares; I would wake up every two hours, swearing I heard banging. My roommates claim to have not heard anything. I passed it off as my growing anxiety. I wish I knew that the anxiety was a symptom, not a cause...

As this continued, I got less and less sleep. I would stay awake for hours - switching from burning hot, sweating and flailing, to freezing cold, shivering and wrapped in my blanket. Then that night happened. I was so tired. I could feel every aching muscle in my body sorely pulling me down to the comfort of my bed. As I wrapped the blankets around me, I listened to the gentle pattering of rain on the sides of the apartment building. Calming me, I closed my eyes. Almost asleep, I felt a heaviness on my back. Thinking it was my cat, I ignored it.

I shouldn’t have ignored it.

Right behind me, whispering in my ear, I heard the raspy male voice that would cut into my soul like daggers. Sadistic, icy, and frightening, I heard these words:

You’re already dead.

I flailed, shooting up faster than lightning. My cat was huddled in a corner. I pulled my knees to my chest and screamed; i couldn’t breathe, I could not think, I could only cry. Finally working up the courage I ran to my computer. I begin typing in voices. Maybe i was going insane? Maybe I was dreaming and didn’t realize it?

The only thing the search returned was a possible hypnagogic experience. I shouldn’t have believed it. I should have left. I should have never come back.

But I did.

A few nights later, I was sleeping soundly, assured it was just my mind.

That’s when I woke up.

My heart lept to my chest. I couldn’t move. I couldn’t breathe. The heavy, icy hands holding me down. My chest felt restricted. I opened my eyes. There, almost lingering over my bed, a shadow.

I couldn’t scream. The creature had its long, decrepit and rotting hands around my neck. I saw its face- ashen flesh hanging onto a black mass, hollow pits where eyes should go, and long, sharp yellowish grey teeth.

It opened its mouth, smiling. The pungent stench of decay hit my face. I wanted to throw up. I wanted to cry. It placed its corpse-like hand over my face.

It went dark.

I awoke the next day. It was as if nothing happened. The doctors said it was just sleep paralysis. They said I was under stress. They gave me some pills to help with the sleeping issue.

I wish they were right.

I wish that I could say that was the end. I wish I could tell you everything was fine after that.

But it wasn’t.

That was just the beginning.

I have to go now. I see the shadow again. I have to get out of here.

Two years ago I was a soldier in the Israeli Air Force and my job wasn't that complex - I repaired and maintained airplanes.

Sometimes, just to break the routine and when manpower was needed, a few soldiers would get picked randomly to go and help some place else. They'd usually pick a group of soldiers and send them together, but for some reason..

They sent me alone.

They sent me to somewhere near Jenin, a Palestinian city near the border. I had to guard the only one road to the city from one side of the border. The job description was pretty straightforward - check if there are any suspicious cars moving on the forbidden territory, report, and if instructed, shoot.

You just sit in the tower, right?

Wrong.

The shifts are two four shifts, I got the nightly one 2-6 (am AND pm). Arriving at 1pm to the camp itself, I started almost right away at 2:00pm. My post stood out like a sore thumb, all the other ones were inside the camp and at a little over ground level. My tower, codenamed Cherry, was at the top of the hill and required me to go up many stairs.

At 1:55pm I put on my vest, my gear, and slowly start climbing up the stairs. It takes me an entire minute to go up the stairs, as there are a lot of them, and the entire post seems very unstable, like it could fall any minute now. It shakes with each step I take.

I finally arrive at the tower and I'm greeted by the guy who was there before me. A tall ginger with a Border Police uniform. He's one of the locals. "Hey, I'm Dan. Take care. See you in eight hours".

The first thing I notice after shaking his hand, were the writings on the walls. They were all over. Before I could ask him about it, he was gone. And just like that, I was alone, for four hours in a tower.

The writings were all similar, but I could tell they were written by different people, as the handwriting was different in almost all of these. All of the writings featured an owl-like creature and were almost always followed by "3:50". We follow a 24 hour clock, so that would mean 3:50 am. Some of the writings would say things like "3:50 is death" and "don't look into it's eyes" while others would swear to never come back here again, ever.

I spent my entire first shift thinking about it, since 3:50am falls during my night hours. What's waiting for me at 3:50? What's all this about? So many questions in my head: What is it? Why is everyone so scared of it? Why was I not briefed about it?

Then came the night shift. As I went up the stairs again, all these questions started racing through my head. All of these questions I could ask Dan about it.

"Hey, good luck out there. Try not to fall asleep, it will attack you". Before I could even open my mouth, Dan ran down the stairs and left me alone in the dark and cold tower.

The 2 am night shift was very different from the day one. You could feel it in the air. The entire atmosphere was different. It was very quiet, almost to an unsettling level. The chilling cold isn't a surface one, it's felt in your bones. This combination of darkness and silence could drive the sanest man crazy at night.

I just sat there and waited. Even with my thick and heavy vest on, it still felt really cold. I waited for what felt like forever. At 3:20, it wasn't funny anymore. At that point, I was more interested in what 'it' was. I no longer cared about the city, so much that I totally forgot about it's existence. I was focused on 3:50.

Then I heard gunshots.

They woke me up from the trance-like state I was in. I jumped in panic and grabbed my gun. "Shots fired, shots fired!" I reported. Some screaming could be heard right after. I was suddenly wide awake, more awake than I had ever been in my life. The rush of adrenaline made me forget all about the cold, or what waited for me at 3:50.

"Relax, it's just some local feud. They sometimes shoot eachother, let the local police deal with it. Not our border, not our problems."

Then at 3:40 I head a horn, specifically a Shofar. It's one of the single things that can scare the shit out of you during daylight, hearing it at night just really almost knocked me off my highchair. And I was pretty sure it was somehow connected to the 3:50 appearance.

It wasn't.

At that point it almost felt like an omen, a sign, like someone told you your time of death, and you're ten minutes away from it waiting for something, and you don't know what. The bitter cold wind blew frighteningly in my face and the chills came back, now colder than ever. I could feel every muscle in my body tense up. It felt like death came creeping. I could feel it in my bones.

And then it started.

At 3:48, an unbearable amount of mosquitoes arrived, I had to fight them off using nothing but my hands. It was pitch black at this hour. I used my cellphone's flash to light the tower up and get all of them away but there were too many of them to number, much less kill.

I was too busy fighting off mosquitoes that I didn't notice what was right in front of me. At a distance no further than a few hundred meters, there it was. It's real. A white creature with glowing eyes coming right towards me, flying at the height of a four story building. It was tall and almost human-like, but had a face that resembled that of an owl.

Instinctively, despite the warnings, I looked it in the eyes.

It's horrifying, deadly eyes.

I could feel the darkness closing in on me, the walls of the tower came closing in. Nowhere to turn, nowhere to run. A sudden obstreperous shriek penetrated me sending shivers down my spine.

Next thing I remember was waking up at 4:12 in serious, almost paralyzing pain. With no recollection of what happened after that. It sounded like a screaming woman, but it was definitely not. That scream scarred me for life, and I can still sometimes hear it in my sleep.

I know most of you probably won't believe me, which is why I took pictures of it. But here is one of the writings on the walls. Another one here. The words next to is say מוות, which means "death" in Hebrew.

It's real, and it's still out there.
